record.paper_title: A solution to an open problem on lower against number in graphs
record.original_question: Let G be a finite connected graph with vertex set V(G), and for each vertex v let N[v] be the closed neighborhood consisting of v and all vertices adjacent to v. A function f from V(G) to {-1, 1} is negative if the sum of f(u) over all u in N[v] is at most 1 for every vertex v. A negative function f is maximal if there is no distinct negative function g such that g(v) is at least f(v) for every vertex v. The lower against number beta_N^*(G) is the minimum value of the total weight sum_{v in V(G)} f(v), taken over all maximal negative functions f. What is the sharp lower bound for beta_N^*(G) for an arbitrary general graph G, expressed in terms of the order of G and the maximum degree of G?

evidence.quote: We solve the problem by establishing a tight lower bound on lower against number of a general graph in terms of order and maximum degree.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite connected graph with vertex set $V(G)$, order $n = |V(G)|$, and maximum degree $\Delta(G)$. For each vertex $v \in V(G)$, let $N[v]$ denote the closed neighborhood of $v$, namely $\{v\} \cup \{u : u \text{ is adjacent to } v\}$. A function $f : V(G) \to \{-1, 1\}$ is called negative if 
$$\sum_{u \in N[v]} f(u) \le 1 \quad \text{for every } v \in V(G).$$
A negative function $f$ is called maximal if there is no negative function $g \ne f$ such that $g(v) \ge f(v)$ for every $v \in V(G)$. Define the lower against number
$$\beta_N^*(G) = \min\Bigl\{\sum_{v \in V(G)} f(v) : f \text{ is a maximal negative function on } G\Bigr\}.$$
Determine the sharp lower bound for $\beta_N^*(G)$ over all finite connected graphs $G$, expressed as a function of the order $n$ and the maximum degree $\Delta(G)$, and characterize when equality holds.
